That is FALSE and I checked it against the tree rather than believing it. Three of my four items were worked in the order I wrote them. `7ad24b4f3` cleared item one's named blocker exactly as instructed and for the right reason -- the drawdown null control was telling the truth and the fixture window was the defect, so it moved the discriminating properties to a constructed book rather than lowering the bar. `5db344a98` registered `figures_on_a_superseded_clock` with both instances consolidated and archived, which was the R10 half of item two and the half that mattered. `537a6f012` closed item three outright with a written, externally-anchored determination. Only EP1 went untouched. The steer is biting; the control that grades it is blind, and it has now graduated from silence to asserting a falsehood in the seat's own brief. THE REAL FAILURE IS ELSEWHERE AND IT IS SERIOUS. The repair for item two was written, is R15-proven both ways, and is in NO COMMIT: 20 files, 1,312 insertions, including `simulation/settlement_clocks.py` (285 lines) and `tests/simulation/test_settlement_clocks.py` (287 lines, parametrised over every scalar in `ROW_DERIVED_SCALARS` so the class reds and not just the two caught figures), sitting staged in the index. Meanwhile the publisher has been wedged 2.4 hours with `episode_failures: 3`, `total_red: 0`, `blocking_tests: []` -- three consecutive `commit_did_not_land` at rc=77 whose own recorded reason is that the scoped suite was GREEN and the commit was refused or timed out. So the live surface still carries the defect: `git show HEAD:site/data/supplier.json` publishes `final_treasury_gbp` 363,283 beside `total_net_gbp` 153,245 on a `starting_treasury_gbp` of 250,000, and 250,000 plus 153,245 is not 363,283. The working tree computes 403,244.79 correctly and no reader can see it. Against the thesis this stretch went forward in understanding and backwards in delivery: the machine diagnosed better than it ships, and a published arithmetic error under the company's name has outlived its own green fix by two and a half hours because the road from a passing test to a reader is broken. The one unambiguous gain is item three, and it is a real one: handed a change that would have tripled its own experiment's population, the machine went to the anchor, found domestic fixed share is a minority in every year of the window (~10-46%, centred near a third), and REFUSED the change on fidelity grounds -- naming the honest repair as a standard-variable product the world does not have, and recording that the honest repair makes the decision surface smaller as a share of the book, not bigger. That is R13 working against the agent's own interest with no one watching, which is the only condition under which it means anything. It also retires the "25 decisions is a plumbing artefact" hope: the surface is bounded near a third of the book by market structure, so the A/B's power problem is real and is not a bug.
